#2472. Rio, 1989: Chilean skullduggery, hidden razor blades and Brazilian flares

The word “skullduggery” is defined as “underhanded or unscrupulous behaviour; trickery”. It has been intertwined with football since time immemorial, exhibited in various degrees. It has been employed by the greats, not least Diego Maradona, and in recent times by compatriot Emiliano Martinez. Players have been banned from tournaments following drug tests and Serie A has been peppered by various instances of a dubious nature. Even the Brazilians are not exempt from employing it, as demonstrated by Rivaldo during the 2002 World Cup.

It should never be a surprise the lengths teams will go to in order to win. And yet it still does. Indeed, the story of Brazil’s 1989 World Cup qualifying campaign involved a classic example of the win-at-all-costs mentality. Sometimes truth is stranger than fiction.

To this day, Brazil hold the amazing record of having qualified for every World Cup finals tournament. They have hosted the tournament twice, but on all other occasions they got through the CONMEBOL qualification process to reach the finals. To imagine them getting eliminated at that stage is almost too much to consider. After all, how do you stop a team like Brazil when you are a smaller South American nation?

In the 1980s, Brazil enjoyed a generation of incredible talent, highlighted by the famous 1982 team containing the likes of Zico, Socrates, Falcao and Eder. Playing attacking football, they charmed the world before becoming unstuck against the Italians on an infamous night in Barcelona.

The loss brought about a period of introspection for the Selecao as they wrestled with balancing their natural attacking game with a more pragmatic European approach to avoid another 1982. Going into the 1986 World Cup, their style changed slightly, with more defensive steel added. They still had a team containing superb strikers such as Careca and Muller, but Zico was 33, Socrates was 32 and Falcao was the same. The 1982 generation was fading from the picture.

Mexico 86 again saw Brazil eliminated by European opposition – this time in the shape of a France team that was also starting to see the end of a golden generation.

Qualification for the 1990 World Cup saw Brazil up against Chile and Venezuela in a three-team round-robin. It was one of three CONMEBOL qualification groups from which the two top teams with the best records would automatically qualify for Italia 90 while the third top team would playoff against a side from the OFC section.

Venezuela had a relatively weak squad and so the group would come down to Chile and Brazil; how they would perform against each other and what goal difference they could rack up against the Venezuelans.

Both teams travelled to Caracas a week apart to start their campaigns, and both came away with comprehensive victories, Brazil 4-0 and Chile 3-1. Brazil’s victory included two goals from Bebeto and one from Romario – a deadly partnership that was beginning to click. That set the stage for the first meeting between the two, which took place in Santiago in August 1989. A win for either team would place them in pole position to win the group.

Tension was high ahead of kick-off. With the game delayed by 15 minutes, the referee insisting on moving back photographers, Romario and defender Alejandro Hisis exchanged words. The striker took offence to something said, Branco having to pull him away before things further.

Within two minutes, the game erupted: Chile could have been down to ten men following a vicious knee-high tackle on Branco by midfielder Raul Ormeno. As Branco was led to the side of the pitch for treatment, a roar from the crowd drew attention to Romario. It appeared that he and Hisis were still feuding, and the camera revealed Romario being followed by three Chileans while Hisis lay on the ground.

The referee showed the PSV striker a straight red and Brazil faced 86 minutes a man short. If anyone wasn’t sure of what exactly had occurred, Romario cleared up the situation after the game: “I didn’t hit him that hard.”

Chile didn’t enjoy a one-man advantage for long. Fourteen minutes into the game Ormeno, who was clearly pumped up, lost the ball to Valdo and brought him down. Immediately realising the consequences, he tried desperately to persuade referee Diaz Palacio to keep his cards in his pocket. It was to no avail. A second yellow card was produced and the Chilean crowd howled as Ormeno had to be escorted off by four teammates. The first half was only a third of the way in.

Scoreless at half-time, Brazil took the lead in the second half through an unfortunate own goal from Hugo Gonzalez. As the game stretched on, it appeared as if Brazil were going to leave Chile with a crucial away victory. But, with just nine minutes remaining, La Roja struck back through a bizarre goal from Ivo Basay.

Brazilian goalkeeper Taffarel had the ball in his area when the referee suddenly decided that he had held it for too long and awarded an indirect free-kick to Chile just four yards from the goal. The quickest Chilean player to react was Jorge Aravena, who touched the ball to Basay to convert.

Brazil were stunned. Chilean fans celebrated on the edge of the pitch, while the Brazilian technical staff went ballistic. There was confusion in every direction but, at the end of 90 minutes, the honours were even, little dividing the two countries in the standings. Brazil were marginally in front on goal difference.

The following week saw O Selecao host Venezuela in Sao Paulo and dish out another lesson, running out 6-0 victors thanks to four goals from Careca, proving that Brazil still had three fearsome strikers to choose from. Seven days later, it was Chile’s turn to host Venezuela and, like the week before, Venezuela were again on the receiving end of a thrashing, this time going down 5-0.

Only one game remained: Brazil against Chile in the Maracana on 3 September 1989. Both teams had two wins and a draw but Brazil’s goal difference was three better than Chile’s. If La Roja were going to eliminate their mighty neighbours and head to Italia 90, they needed to win in Rio. It would be a tough ask, but at least they were in a position where it was a possibility.

Get an early goal and maybe the Brazilians would start to tense up in front of an expectant crowd. And let’s not forget that Brazil had suffered unexpected heartache at the Maracana before, losing the 1950 final to Uruguay. It was game on for that World Cup berth. But the Selecao had also never lost a World Cup qualification game in its history.

In front of a huge crowd of over 140,000, the two sides took to the pitch. Brazil would be without Romario – still suspended following the previous meeting’s sending-off – but with Careca and Bebeto upfront, they looked strong. Unfortunately for Chile, they would be without star striker Ivan Zamorano, who was unable to make it back from his Swiss side, Neuchatel Xamax, in time. The game was going to require an experienced referee, which it got in the shape of Argentine Juan Carlos Loustau.

The last time Chile had beaten Brazil was a famous 4-0 win during the 1987 Copa America, and many of the team were in this side. Unsurprisingly, given the stakes, the early minutes were once again physical. Chilean left-back Hector Puebla left his studs on the knee of Mauro Galvao after just four minutes, although the referee didn’t blow for a foul. Then, just two minutes later, Bebeto tricked Puebla, who brought the Brazilian down and then appeared to stamp on his thigh. This time the referee saw fit to show Puebla a yellow card to calm the Chilean down.

The game continued with Brazil enjoying most of the possession but Chile remaining disciplined in defence. Although it was Chile who needed the win, they seemed focused on trying to reach half-time without conceding, rather than attempting to score. Brazil were creating chances, especially through Careca, but goalkeeper Roberto Rojas was equal to everything. Whenever Chile did venture into the Brazilian half, they were usually swiftly dispossessed.

With Chile sitting deep, most of Brazil’s efforts were from distance – they were having difficulty penetrating the tight defence. Just before half-time, Branco hit a hard, swerving shot that Rojas did well to adjust to and save. And with that, the teams went into the break still scoreless.

Brazil started the second half where they had left off previously – on the attack. And finally, four minutes in, they broke the deadlock. A defensive header from Branco fell to Dunga who played a quick ball forward to Bebeto. Spinning towards goal, he cleared one challenge before hitting a through ball to Careca. The Napoli star sidestepped Puebla before hitting a shot that, although partially saved by Rojas, went in. Brazil were 1-0 up and heading for Italia 90. Chile were facing elimination.

For the following five minutes, Chile dominated as they tried desperately to get back into the tie. Brazil weathered the storm before taking control once again. It was impossible to see where Chile would get two goals from, which would mean committing men forward, leaving gaps for Bebeto and Careca to exploit. Then came the dramatic moment of the game.

On 68 minutes, Chile had possession of the ball in their own half through Astengo when a huge roar suddenly burst out from the crowd. TV cameras swivelled across to goalkeeper Rojas who lay in his penalty area while something flamed and smoked beside him. As the cameras lingered, it appeared as though a flare had been thrown by someone, Chilean players rushing to Rojas’ aid. As they understood what had happened, tempers began to rise. Patricio Yanez made several obscene gestures at the Brazilian fans.

The Chileans motioned for a stretcher but, with none immediately forthcoming, took the initiative and carried their stricken goalkeeper off the field. The cameras showed blood running down the back of Rojas’ head as he was carried down the stairs into the tunnel, along with his teammates.

The stunned Brazilian players discussed what to do next with the referee, spending a further 20 minutes on the pitch awaiting the return of the Chileans. Eventually, the referee was forced to abandon the game, meaning that the likely solution would be a replay at a neutral venue. It appeared that Brazil had been just 22 minutes from Italy before their unruly fans ruined the day.

As mentioned, the TV cameras had swivelled to Rojas after the crowd noise drew attention to the incident. There was no footage of Rojas being hit by the flare, just his injured body writhing in agony on the floor. But one pitchside photographer, Paulo Teixeira, had seen the flare come onto the field – and something struck him as not quite right.

He could see Rojas bleeding from near his eye but was sure that the flare had landed many feet away from him. In a CNN interview, he recalled his immediate reaction: “I missed the shot and so did most of the photographers. But there was one guy by me, Ricardo Alfieri, a good friend, and I asked him, ‘Ricardo, did you capture the flare?’ He said, ‘Of course, about 4-5 shots.'”

Alfieri worked for a Japanese publication and so had to send his unprocessed film to them the next morning. Teixeira realised that he needed to move fast if his gut instinct was correct. Finding a local radio reporter, he convinced him to put Alfieri on air, who told listeners that he had shots that showed the flare had not struck Rojas.

Immediately after, the Brazilian football president, Ricardo Teixeira, came to the station and asked about the film. Together, they found a local lab and, dragging a poor technician out on a Sunday night, had her warm the lab up for the next four hours. Finally, they were able to process Alfieri’s film.

Teixeira takes up the story again. “When the pictures came out, there were four clear shots – starting with the device flying and then landing one meter away from Rojas. [CBF president] Teixeira was so relieved.”

The photos were published the next day by local news agency Globo while CBF President Teixeira flew to FIFA’s headquarters in Switzerland. There was clear evidence now that the flare had not directly injured Rojas. But if that was the case, what had caused the bleeding seen on his head?

Two days on from the game, the medical report from the incident stated that there had been no burn marks on Rojas, just a cut on the left side of his forehead. Now back in Santiago, Rojas released a statement saying that he was shocked that people were doubting the nature of his injury.

Rojas’ club side, Sao Paulo, were also publicly expressing doubts about keeping him on the books Finally, five days later, FIFA came to their decision: due to the lack of burn marks and Chile refusing to play on, the game was awarded to Brazil by a 2-0 margin. The Selecao had qualified for yet another World Cup.

But the mystery hadn’t been settled. Had a Brazilian thrown the firecracker? And how did the wound on the forehead arise? The first question was soon solved. It had been thrown by a Brazilian, a 24-year-old woman by the name of Rosenery Mello. After she was named in the press, she became a minor celebrity, leading to a cover pose in the November 1989 Brazilian edition of Playboy and the nickname “Maracana Rocket”.

The reason for her decision to appear on the cover? The CBF had fined her $12,000 for throwing the flare, while she was allegedly getting $40,000 for the cover.

So now we knew where the flare came from that missed Rojas, but we still didn’t know what had caused the wound. The answer finally came out when Rojas was questioned further in the ensuing days.

He had concealed a razor blade in his glove ahead of the match in order to simulate injury should the need arise. Just think about that for a minute – a professional player had decided before a vital World Cup qualifier to have a blade ready with which to cut himself should he feel it was necessary.

Incredibly, this wasn’t something Rojas had cooked up himself; both manager Orlando Aravena and team doctor Daniel Rodriguez were also involved. The whole scheme had, in fact, been concocted in the training camp to get the game abandoned at any sign of crowd trouble or player fighting.

Unsurprisingly, Rojas was given a lifetime ban from the game, which was finally rescinded in 2001, allowing him to return to Sao Paulo as a goalkeeping coach and then manager. Chile were also barred from the 1994 World Cup qualification process, although more because of abandoning the game than the injury simulation.

Both Aravena and Rodriguez, along with the president of the Chilean football federation, Sergio Stoppel, and the captain, Fernando Astengo, were punished by FIFA. Astengo has protested his innocence to this day, swearing he had no knowledge of the plan.

This is not the only example over the years of what might be termed an “overreaction” to objects thrown from the crowd during a game. Of course, any such action by fans is deplorable and it is only natural that they should suffer sanctions But that has not prevented such actions sometimes being milked by the victims. The two best-known examples are probably the infamous Borussia Monchengladbach Coke can and the Celtic bottle.

The Coke can incident occurred during the 1971/72 European Cup when Borussia Monchengladbach hosted Inter. With the Germans leading 2-1, Inter legend Roberto Boninsegna seemed to be hit on the head by an object, suddenly falling to the ground.

The object turned out to be a Coke can. Gladbach’s Gunter Netzer had his wits about him and disposed of the offending item, before Sandro Mazzola grabbed another from a fan and presented it to the referee. The upshot was that Gladbach won 7-1, but Inter managed to persuade UEFA to annul the game and replay it. Inter ended up proceeding to the final against Ajax.

The second incident occurred when Celtic hosted Rapid Wien in the 1984/85 Cup Winners’ Cup. In a game that was already boiling over as Celtic took a 3-0 lead saw a penalty awarded to the Bhoys. As the Austrian players argued with the referee, a bottle was thrown onto the pitch from the Celtic crowd.

Like the Brazilian flare, it missed everyone, but that didn’t stop Rapid’s Rudi Weinhofer from collapsing, holding his face before being taken off, his head heavily bandaged by the physio. Like Gladbach, Celtic were ordered to replay the game at a neutral venue – Old Trafford – and also were eliminated.

But both incidents were just feigning injury; they were not quite at the scale of concealing and then cutting yourself with a razor. And the truth is that, had it not been due to the quick thinking of a Brazilian photojournalist, Chile may have succeeded. Nowadays, such a rouse would be impossible given all the camera angles and mobile phone footage. But back then, it was a different ballgame.

To paraphrase the Scooby Doo series, “Chile would have gotten away with it if it wasn’t for those meddling photographers.” It is a funny old game, indeed.

#2471. Un doublé pour Luis Sanchez

Il y a deux jours, l'ancien éphémère Vert (2019-2020), Luis Francisco Sánchez Mosquera, qui opère désormais, depuis cet été, dans le club colombien du Deportes Tolima, basé à Ibagué s'est illustré à l'occasion de la 17ème journée du championnat de clôture sur le terrain du Deportivo Pereira. Deportes Tolima l'a emporté par 3 à 1 et Luis Francisco Sánchez Mosquera a inscrit un doublé aux 13ème et 16ème minutes. Parti de son propre camp, il a percé plein axe et décoché, des 25 mètres, un tir au sol au ras du poteau pour le premier. Quant au deuxième, il l'a inscrit en reprenant un centre en retrait à l'intérieur de la surface de réparation.

Luis Francisco Sánchez Mosquera, l'un des trois Sanchez passés par l'ASSE, après Daniel (1983-1985) et Christophe (2000-2001) poursuit sa carrière en Colombie. Après avoir fait sa formation au CD America Cali, Luis Francisco Sánchez Mosquera, milieu de terrain offensif, intègre l'équipe première et joue 16 rencontres (2buts) alors qu'il a tout juste 19 ans. Repéré par l'ASSE, il arrive chez les Verts, à l'âge de 19 ans, le 22 août 2019, en prêt pour deux saisons, pour, dans un premier temps renforcer le groupe de N2 de Razik Nedder. Une option d'achat au terme du prêt dans l'accord avait été incluse. Il faisait également partie de la sélection U20 de Colombie. Sélectionné pour la Coupe du monde de cette catégorie, il avait dû renoncer à y participer à cause d'une blessure. Son passage à l'ASSE sera un échec. En effet Luis Francisco Sánchez Mosquera n'aura porté que huit mois le maillot vert de la réserve et retournera en Colombie dès le printemps 2020.

Après son départ de l'ASSE, il va passer 4 saisons au CD America Cali qui le transfère le 5 juin 2024 au Central Cordoba, un club argentin. Il y reste 6 mois et est transféré, en janvier 2025, à Fortaleza CEIF qui, en juillet 2025, le prête à Once Caldas, avant donc de le transférer au Club Deportes Tolima.

#2470. Remembering the disaster of 1991/92, Bayern Munich’s worst season in modern history

Mention the words ‘Bayern Munich’ and what comes to mind? A teutonic powerhouse? One of Europe’s elite? Serial winners? The Bavarians are, after all, a team that has won the Bundesliga 31 times – when the first was only 55 years ago.

It is a team that has won the European Cup six times and includes such notable alumni as Franz Beckenbauer, Gerd Muller, Sepp Maier, Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, Lothar Matthaus and Philipp Lahm. It is a world-famous brand that stands for excellence. Bayern Munich equals trophies and success.

But hard as it is to believe, they have endured ups and downs just like all teams – the difference being that a Bayern “down” is still normally what most other teams dream about.

But there is one season that will always live in infamy in Bayern history, a season during the 1990s when they were, frankly speaking, pretty terrible. Of course, terrible for Die Roten is relative – we are not talking about relegation here – but by their lofty standards, they turned into a mediocre team for 12 months. The season in question took place across 1991/92.

What’s more surprising is that there was no immediate sign beforehand of the slump to come. The 1986/87 campaign had seen an Udo Lattek-led Bayern win the Bundesliga, the manager whom Die Roten had dominated Europe under in the 1970s.

That proved to be his final season before being replaced by Jupp Heynckes, who ironically had also replaced Lattek when he became Borussia Monchengladbach manager in 1979. While unable to replicate the Foals’ amazing 1970s success, Heynckes did lead them to fourth-place finishes in 1985 and 1986, followed by third place in 1987 along with a UEFA Cup semi-final, putting him on Bayern’s radar.

Heynckes’ debut season (1987/88) saw Bayern fail to retain their title as an emergent Werder Bremen secured glory under the stewardship of Otto Rehhagel. With strikers Karl-Heinz Riedle and Frank Neubarth, and a defence that conceded just 22 goals in 34 games, Bremen finished four points ahead of second-place Bayern, having beaten them 3-1 in a key week 26 meeting. But normal service was soon resumed as Bayern lifted the Bundesliga the following year while also reaching the semi-finals of the UEFA Cup.

The 1989/90 season saw Bayern even more dominant, again winning the Bundesliga by six points while this time reaching the semi-finals of the European Cup, before falling to the AC Milan of the three Dutch masters. Looking at the squad that season, it is notable that there were no world-renowned stars. The strike duo of Roland Wohlfarth and Alan McInally, while efficient, were hardly names that would’ve had Baresi, Maldini and co worried. But it was still enough to dominate Germany.

As such, the summer of 1990 saw Heynckes strengthen the squad by bringing in Stefan Effenberg, Brian Laudrup and Christian Ziege. Of these, the signing of Effenberg was by far the most interesting. A player who throughout his career would be no stranger to controversy, he was asked about why he had decided to join Bayern. Sporting his blonde mullet, he replied, “Because the other clubs are too stupid to win the Bundesliga.”

It was a surefire way to place a target on your back for the season, a comment sure to have been posted on opposing dressing room walls, including Kaiserslautern’s. An early season league game saw Bayern hammer Kaiserslautern 4-0 at the Olympiastadion before the season then developed into a battle between both teams for the title.

Late March saw the advantage swing to Kaiserslautern as they defeated Bayern 2-1 at home courtesy of a late winner from Stefan Kuntz. That sparked a strong run from Die Roten and, with three matches to go, things were tight.

Bayern then travelled to Bochum to face little-fancied Wattenscheid – a team that played in the tiny Lohrheidestadion and who Bayern had beaten 7-0 earlier in the season. To the shock of a watching nation, Wattenscheid held a 2-1 lead as the game entered the dying minutes. Then, with just three minutes left, the ever-reliable Wohlfarth scored to save Bayern’s blushes. Or so it seemed.

Two minutes later, Thorsten Fink scored a shock winner for the team from Bochum to send 35,000 fans delirious – a defeat that opened the door for Kaiserslautern to claim their first Bundesliga title.

As if the defeat to Wattenscheid wasn’t painful enough, Bayern also suffered heartache in the European Cup. Once again, the semi-final curse raised its head, this time to Eastern European opposition rather than Italian. A strong team had emerged at Red Star Belgrade, who came to Munich and left with a 2-1 win in the first leg of their semi-final clash.

That left Bayern with a tough assignment in front of 80,000 rabid Red Star fans – flares burning in an intimidating atmosphere. But Die Roten rose to the task and the game was about to enter extra-time with Bayern 2-1 up when a freak own goal from captain Klaus Augenthaler in the last minute saw the Yugoslavs grab the all-important equaliser and move on to the final.

So as 1991/92 commenced, Bayern came off disappointment at the end of the preceding season but had still finished second in the league and narrowly missed on a European Cup final appearance. It was a season that many teams would die for.

The squad development continued as Heynckes brought in players such as Jan Wouters, Oliver Kreuzer, Thomas Berthold and two Brazilians, Mazinho and Bernardo. But balancing that was the retirement of long-serving stalwart Augenthaler. Still, Bayern fans were looking forward to reclaiming their position at the top of the league while perhaps claiming a UEFA Cup title.

The opening two league games saw an inauspicious start as Bayern drew at Werder Bremen before losing at home to Bundesliga new boys Hansa Rostock. They then travelled to Dusseldorf and came away with their first win, albeit only 1-0 thanks to a last-minute winner from Mazinho. Fans could start to relax ahead of a straightforward cup tie at home against minnows FC Homburg.

Homburg is a small town in the Saarland region of Germany and their local team had been relatively obscure for most of its history. But, in 1986, they had reached the Promised Land of the Bundesliga for the first time. Their fans enjoyed two seasons at the top table before being relegated and then returning immediately. And so, travelling to Munich, the team was a second-tier outfit who typically played in front of 8,000 fans, even when in the Bundesliga.

Only 9,000 bothered to trek to the Olympiastadion to watch the tie, resulting in a strange atmosphere within the vast bowl. It took 27 minutes but Bayern grabbed the lead through a backpost header from Mazinho. So far, so good. But Homburg emerged in the second half revitalised and had the cheek to equalise via a powerful shot from Rodolfo Cardoso.

Worse was to come for Bayern as, with just 13 minutes remaining, a loose ball fell to Homburg’s Matthias Baranowski, who gladly accepted the gift. This was not in the Bayern script and could not be permitted. Unsurprisingly, while Homburg fans were still rubbing their eyes, Mazinho scored again. Enough of this nonsense.

And so the game went into extra-time when Bayern’s fitness would surely overwhelm the underdogs. But just five minutes in, Homburg’s Michael Kimmel jinked into the area and scored with a low shot. That pesky Homburg side just didn’t know when to lie down. And if that wasn’t bad enough, they then scored again four minutes later through Bernd Gries. Bayern were 4-2 down at home. That was how the game would end. A shocked Bayern had been eliminated in their first cup game by a lower division team in their own stadium.

Sometimes a cup defeat can be a blessing in disguise – at least now they could focus on the league and UEFA Cup. Maybe all was not lost yet.

Their league form continued to fluctuate and, after nine matches, Bayern sat in seventh place as they prepared to commence their continental campaign. A relatively easy first-round draw saw them due to travel to Ireland for a first leg against Cork City. As Bayern fans researched where Cork was on the map, the players flew over.

Cork City had only formed in 1984, following the bankruptcy of Cork United in 1982. A second-place league finish in the previous season had seen the part-timers earn their spot in the UEFA Cup. In front of just 4,000 fans, it was time for Bayern to forget about the Homburg embarrassment and start a successful UEFA Cup campaign.

Dave Barry was a local who enjoyed a successful career with Cork County, playing Gaelic Football and winning two All-Ireland medals. But he also enjoyed regular football on the side and so turned out for Cork City as a midfielder. Ahead of the game, he had somehow come to the attention of Effenberg who, with his normal diplomacy, compared him to his grandfather.

Picked for the game against Bayern, he wrote his name into Irish folklore when, after just 26 minutes, Cork stole the ball from the advancing Bayern defence and Barry found it at his feet. Charging forward, the balding midfielder turned inside one defender before rifling a shot home. The fans went ballistic.

And so it stood until just before half-time when Effenberg finally brought parity to the score. Everyone then braced for the second-half whirlwind from Bayern, but it never occurred. The part-timers of Cork ended with a famous 1-1 draw against the German giants.

The second leg saw Bayern struggle once more. In fact, the Irish part-timers held out until the 71st minute before Bruno Labbadia finally spared Bayern’s blushes. A last-gasp penalty added a little more gloss, but at the final whistle, Die Roten had only just got over the line. Considering this and the Homburg result, all was most definitely not well in Bavaria.

Three days later, Bayern travelled to Stuttgart and were hammered 4-1 – not by VfB but rather by Stuttgarter Kickers. It was finally too much to bear and, three days later, Bayern announced that they were parting company with Heynckes.

The former striking great went on to enjoy a long and successful managerial career, overseeing teams in Spain, Portugal and Germany, including Real Madrid, Benfica, Schalke and his first love, Borussia Monchengladbach. He even returned to Bayern, becoming caretaker manager in 2009 after the firing of Jurgen Klinsmann before replacing Louis van Gaal in 2011 and leading them to a Champions League final defeat to Chelsea.

He then giuded Bayern to glory in 2013 by defeating Bundesliga rivals Borussia Dortmund in the final, making Heynckes just the fourth manager to win the competition with two different teams, Real Madrid being the other. One of the all-time greats, his dismissal after the Kickers defeat was later described by general manager Uli Hoeness as “the biggest mistake I ever made in my business life”.

A meeting was set up with club legend Franz Beckenbauer in Munich’s Sheraton Hotel to offer him the position as head coach. But he declined, stating prior commitments made it impossible. And therefore Bayern turned elsewhere – with a somewhat surprising result.

Replacing Heynckes at the helm would be Danish legend Soren Lerby. A player who enjoyed three seasons with Bayern, during which they won two Bundesliga titles, he had only recently retired from playing at the age of 32. Taking the Bayern job represented his first step into management – a daunting task for experienced heads let alone a rookie. He didn’t even have the required coaching licence at the time of his appointment. It seemed a strange choice to most fans.

His tenure started off shakily as Bayern lost successive league games against Dortmund and VfB Stuttgart to drop to 14th in the 20-team league, just three places above the relegation spots. Next up for Lerby was, ironically, a trip back to Denmark as Bayern had drawn Boldklubben 1903 in the second round of the UEFA Cup. If Lerby thought it would be an enjoyable trip home, he was in for a major surprise.

Not even the most hardcore Boldklubben fans can claim that their team had a grand history. They had won the league seven times, but four of those were before World War Two, while the most recent was back in 1976, before then merging with Kjobenhavns Boldklub in 1992 to form FC Copenhagen, who have enjoyed considerable success since.

They had only ever won two European ties and never made it past the second round. The visit of Bayern would represent one of the last games that Boldklubben would play before the merger. And what a game it was.

Over 14,000 fans packed into the Gentofte Stadion to see how their boys would fare against the German powerhouse. For 30 minutes the game was a stalemate, until Bayern snatched the lead through Mazinho. That lead lasted just five minutes before Michael Manniche tied the game. Tied going into the half-time break, there was little indication of the shockwave to come.

After 57 minutes, Boldklubben earned a penalty, which was duly dispatched by Danish star Ivan Nielsen. Four minutes later, the fans were in ecstasy as Kenneth Wegner made it 3-1. As the ground began to shake, the madness continued; just three minutes later, Manniche grabbed a second to put the Danes 4-1 up. The mighty Bayern had just conceded three goals in the space of seven minutes. And it wasn’t over yet.

Brian Klaus added a fifth before Peter Uldbjerg made it 6-1. No-one could quite believe what they were witnessing. Markus Munch pulled back a last-minute consolation for Bayern but, as the final whistle sounded, all eyes turned to the scoreboard: Boldklubben 1903 6-2 Bayern Munich. Bayern’s season had just truly imploded.

The return leg two weeks later saw Die Roten exit the competition with a whimper, winning just 1-0 through a late Mazinho goal. They had now been eliminated from the DFB-Pokal at home by a lower division side, from the UEFA Cup by Danish minnows and were sitting in 14th place in the league.

Given this start, it was no real surprise that Lerby was a dead man walking. He managed to stumble on until March when a 4-0 defeat away at Kaiserslautern saw Bayern, still stuck in the lower half of the table, finally wield the axe. It was to represent Lerby’s only stint in football management.

It was time for a third manager that season as Hoeness turned to a much more experienced hire in Erich Ribbeck.

Ribbeck had started his managerial career back in 1967 at Rot-Weiss Essen before managing Eintracht Frankfurt, Kaiserslautern, Borussia Dortmund and Bayer Leverkusen. His stats to date were at best mediocre – the only trophy he won during that period was the UEFA Cup with Bayer Leverkusen in 1988 – but he had Bundesliga experience and so was seen as the man who could right the listing ship.

But Bayern by now were in a complete funk and so Ribbeck oversaw a final 11 league games in which they won five but lost as many as they stumbled over the finishing line, mired in mediocrity.

With the season over, Bayern sat in tenth, exactly mid-table. They had lost more games than they had won, including seven at home, and finished with a -2 goal difference. As usual, Wohlfarth was top scorer with 17, followed by Mazinho (12) and Effenberg (11). They had to sit back and watch while VfB Stuttgart, Dortmund and Frankfurt played out final-day drama to captivate the whole country.

All three teams sat on 50 points going into the final matchday and all three were playing away from home. Frankfurt had goal difference advantage and just needed to win, but shockingly lost to Hansa Rostock while having a clear penalty denied to them at 1-1.

Dortmund won at Duisburg and were two minutes from being Bundesliga champions before Guido Buchwald wrote himself into Stuttgart legend with an 88th-minute winner at Leverkusen – despite being down to ten men following the sending-off of Matthias Sammer – earning Stuttgart the title on goal difference.

That summer saw Bayern spend big. In came Thomas Helmer, Jorginho, Mehmet Scholl and, most newsworthy, the return of the prodigal son, Lothar Matthaus. Laudrup and Effenberg were moved on to Fiorentina to help fund the rebuild.

It worked: Bayern finished second in the Bundesliga, just a point behind champions Werder Bremen and with just five losses and a +29 goal difference. Ribbeck had successfully steadied the ship and would soon retire, replaced by Beckenbauer before a disastrous spell as Germany manager from 1998 to 2000. But Ribbeck also left with the unenviable stat of becoming the first and only manager of Bayern to be in charge for over 500 days without winning a single trophy.

To this day, the 1991/92 season stands as a nadir for Bayern. Since the, Die Roten have only ever finished outside the top three twice, and have won 12 Bundesliga titles and three Champions Leagues. While 90s was often an inconsistent decade for Bayern – with players more often featured in the gossip pages rather than the sports pages, leading to the famous “FC Hollywood” nickname – nothing was as bad as 1991/92.

Bayern will always represent one of the elite European teams and are the gold standard against which many others measure themselves. Moreover, they have enjoyed success without the huge external financial backing that some other European sides have enjoyed.

It has been argued by many that their recent dominance of German football has spoilt the Bundesliga as a spectacle, especially considering their ten successive. But it is refreshing to know that even teams like Bayern Munich can experience a season of woe. For that one year, they were actually human after all. And for that, VfB Stuttgart, Homborg, Cork City and Boldklubben will be eternally grateful.

#2468. Rumilly-Vallières est d'attaque

Ex-adjoint de David Guion et de Pierre Sage à Chambéry, l'actuel entraîneur du GFA Rumilly-Vallières (qui recevra l'ASSE à Annecy le dimanche 15 novembre à 15h00 lors du 7e tour de Coupe de France), Cédric Rullier a commenté aujourd'hui sur le site de la FFF les impressionnantes stats offensives de son équipe, de loin la plus prolifique tous groupes confondus en National 1 (27 buts en 8 rencontres soit une moyenne de 3,4 pions claqués par match).

"Marquer autant, cela ne m'était jamais arrivé. Mais on a une recette qui fonctionne bien pour former des attaquants ! Déjà, l'an passé, avec Sabri Hattab, on avait le meilleur buteur de notre poule (16 buts). Je ne veux pas dissocier l'aspect collectif de l'aspect individuel. Le joueur, quand il arrive chez nous, entre dans un projet collectif. On va d'abord regarder l'homme. Ensuite, il doit s'adapter à notre projet de jeu et enfin, il y a tout ce qui entre en compte dans le secteur de la performance : la tactique, la technique, le travail devant le but que l'on fait beaucoup... On bosse aussi avec des outils comme des préférences motrices. D'ailleurs, l'un des coachs s'occupe du développement individuel de chaque joueur avec des axes d'amélioration très précis. On a aussi un préparateur mental, on travaille beaucoup sur la confiance en soi. En fait, on choisit les joueurs et après, on les place dans un système.

Sur les 27 buts marqués, 11 l'ont été par des joueurs différents. Arrivé du Clermont Foot, l'avant-centre Amine Saïd a inscrit 6 buts. Notre ailier Maxence Fortier en a marqué 5. Samedi dernier Maxence était remplaçant au coup d'envoi et il a mis un quadruplé. A Châteauroux, lors du match précédent, il avait délivré trois passes décisives et Amine avait marqué trois buts. C'est bien la preuve que ça tient au collectif. Chaque semaine, à chaque entraînement, on travaille la finition. Pour moi, tous les joueurs doivent être capables de marquer, aussi bien mes défenseurs centraux sur coups de pied arrêtés que mes latéraux. Ils doivent s'inscrire dans ce projet collectif. C'est pour ça qu'on a beaucoup de buteurs différents.

Je ne veux pas dépendre d'un buteur unique. Tant mieux si on a le meilleur buteur de la poule mais ça reste fragile, imaginons qu'il se blesse ou qu'il parte... Chaque fin de saison, nos meilleurs attaquants partent mais certains, pour moi, ont stagné. Chez nous, le système les fait progresser, et quand ils partent, parfois un peu trop vite à mon goût mais c'est leur choix et je le respecte, ils ne sont plus du tout dans le même système. Nous, au GFA, on se créé beaucoup d'occasions, donc quelque part c'est normal que l'on marque beaucoup. Souvent, nos adversaires changent d'organisation parce qu'ils voient que l'on marque beaucoup. Ils sont attentifs à ça. Mais à l'inverse, on encaisse trop de buts (13 en 8 matches) et les joueurs en ont conscience.

On a un jeu assez ouvert. Pour moi, le foot doit rester un spectacle et créer une émotion. Quand on est enfant, on veut arrêter un tir ou marquer des buts, c'est ça qui fait que le foot est ludique. On se souvient plus des finales de Ligue des champions avec des gros scores, non ? C'est ma vision du foot, je suis tourné vers ça : se créer des occasions, marquer des buts... Au GFA, on travaille pour ça. C'est de bon augure, surtout que l'on doit avoir le 8e ou le 10e budget de la poule, et que l'on est l'une des plus petites agglomérations avec 17 000 habitants à Rumilly et 3000 à Vallières. Cela ne représente pas grand-chose si l'on compare à des communes comme Tours, Toulon, Hyères, Nîmes, Fréjus, Bourges et même Châteauroux. Mais ce qui fait aussi notre force, c'est que l'on est un club stable, à tous les niveaux, et c'est agréable."

#2465. Esteban Mouton content de revenir dans le Chaudron

Supporter des Verts et formé à l'ASSE, le défenseur lavallois Esteban Mouton (23 ans) s'est confié à Ouest-France avant de défier les leaders stéphanois demain soir à Geoffroy-Guichard. Extraits.

"On joue au foot pour ces matches-là. Il y aura la famille et les copains. Cette fois-ci, je serai de l’autre côté et c’est très sympa de revenir dans ce stade dont j'ai arpenté les tribunes quand j'étais jeune. Je n'ai pas été conservé par Sainté mais cet échec m'a forgé. J'ai alors démarré un nouveau périple de 5 ans. Du R1 et une montée avec l’Olympique Valence en 2023 jusqu’à la lutte pour la montée en L2 avec Orléans la saison dernière, entrecoupés par une accession puis un maintien en National à Aubagne. J’ai passé les étapes crescendo.

Je suis monté d’un niveau presque chaque année. Je suis très heureux d’avoir du temps de jeu en Ligue 2. L’arrivée du coach David Vignes n’a fait que confirmer mon choix. Je savais qu’il allait prôner un jeu attractif, assez offensif. C’est mon profil, même si j’ai plein de choses à gommer sur le côté défensif. Son système en 4-4-2 losange est assez hybride, on bouge beaucoup. Je trouve que c’est assez sympa, parce que ça met aussi l’adversaire en difficulté et quand on le maîtrise bien, c’est un système qui peut-être très performant.

Je prends du plaisir, je joue. Techniquement et physiquement, on se met rapidement au diapason de tout le monde. J’ai toujours fonctionné comme ça à chaque division franchie. On est resté soudé depuis le début en travaillant très bien. La victoire face à Boulogne est venue récompenser les dernières semaines. La clé, ce sera de jouer avec nos qualités sans trop penser à la suite. Saint-Étienne est une très bonne équipe. Ils ne sont pas premiers pour rien mais on a vu qu’ils se sont fait embêter par Guingamp à l’extérieur. À nous de profiter de cette dynamique pour aller chercher des points."

#2464. SC Freiburg vs. Union Berlin preview: Freiburg look to continue title push against struggling Union

Ironically, the 640km separating Berlin and Freiburg im Breisgau is a pretty accurate representation of where the teams currently sit on the table: with a win, Freiburg can push their way back into 3rd place as they continue hunting for a UEFA Champions League spot and maintain their pressure on Dortmund and Bayern, while Union Berlin could potentially sink back down into the relegation zone depending on Schalke’s outcome.

Will we see a shock at the Europa-Park Stadion, or will we see the points gap between both sides continue to widen?

Let’s begin with the home side, SC Freiburg.

Freiburg have been on a burner to commence the 2026/27 season with 5 wins, 3 draws and a solitary loss only coming against champions Bayern München, along with a respectable +8GD (18 goals scored). In addition to this, Freiburg ensured their Pokal survival by staving off recently relegated Wolfsburg with a last-gasp winner by Keisuke Gotō. The team from Baden-Württemberg also had a healthy start to their Conference League campaign with 2 wins and 1 loss, their most recent result being a 1-0 away win against Trabzonspor.

To go back to the Bundesliga, Freiburg managed to overcome a 1-0 deficit to Augsburg to come away from Bavaria with a 2-1 win in their most recent match. A win against Union Berlin would see them not only move back up to 3rd, but also come to within 2 points of league leaders Borussia Dortmund and Bayern München.

Apart from their 3-1 loss to Bayern München, Freiburg have been otherwise flawless at home and look poised to strike while the iron’s hot as they push for a first-ever UCL qualification.

A duo to watch this match will certainly be the strike partnership of Igor Matanović and Yuito Suzuki, who account for 8 goals (4 goals each) - nearly half of Freiburg’s total goals this season.

SC Freiburg will be without Florent Muslija and Patrick Osterhage.

Ironically, the club known as “Eisern Union” (Iron Union) seem to have let their iron cool down as they sit near the bottom of the table as one of the league's most out of form teams.

Since shocking the footballing world by qualifying for the UCL in the 2022/23 season, Union Berlin has in fact looked quite malleable in recent seasons (I promise that’s the last metal-related joke I will make!), with this season shaping up to be a relegation survival battle for the Berliners.

With only 1 win in 8 games thus far (4D, 3L), Union squandered their previous Bundesliga matchup against 1. FC Köln at home, losing out on some much needed points with direct relegation rivals. This followed a 5-0 battering by that very same Köln team in the Pokal less than a week prior.

The bad news for Union continues if we look at their away form thus far - in just 3 matches, Union has drawn 1 and lost 2, with a shocking -11 goal differential (1 scored, 12 conceded), by far the worst in the league.

With local rivals Hertha Berlin having just beaten top-of-the-table rivals Wolfsburg and continuing their flawless run in the 2. Bundesliga (10W, 1D, and a +16 GD), the pressure is surely beginning to mount on Union securing their status as Berlin’s best team.

Union Berlin will miss the likes of Andrej Iic, Stanley Nsoki, Andrik Markgraf and Robert Skov. Felix Uduokhai remains out via suspension after his red card against Augsburg.

To give Union fans a bit of hope, Freiburg have had a shaky record in recent years against the team from Berlin.

Union have been flawless against Freiburg in their last 7 matches (4 wins, 3 draws, and outscoring Freiburg 9:4), with their last loss occurring nearly 4 years ago to the day. Union is also currently on a 2-game winning streak against Freiburg when playing in the Europa-Park Stadion.

This does come with a caveat however, which is that both sides were a lot closer in regards to form and table positioning in the same fixture last season - in 2025/26, Freiburg was 8th (34 points, -5 GD) while Union was 11th (28 points, -12 GD). This time, 16th place Union (7 points, -12 GD) will really have to punch up if they want to win against 4th place Freiburg (16 points, +8 GD).

If Union Berlin are to regain their form, perhaps they can make it happen against Freiburg and potentially eke out another win to pick up some much needed points and create some separation at the bottom of the table.

Au-delà des victoires, les hommes d’Herbin sont restés invaincus dans le Chaudron durant 4 ans ½ entre mars 1973 et août 1977 !

#2457. Ch-ch-ch-ch Changes !

On a beau porter le nom d’une mythique relique, on a beau fièrement afficher des valeurs en marge de la toile putacliquesque, on n’a rien contre un brin de toilette. Il faut vivre avec son temps dit l’adage. Alors poteaux-carrés évolue (sous vos yeux qu’on espère ébahis).

Né en 2005, époque où les Verts de Juju, Hellebuyck, Cartoche, Compan et Janot retrouvaient la D1 tandis que leurs supporters se déchiraient entre pro Anto et pro Bozzo, poteaux-carrés se voulait alors résolument passionné, indépendant, frondeur et rieur.

Le Furan a sinué dans les entrailles de Sainté, ce qui sera toujours plus glamour qu'une pâle eau coulant sous d'anonymes ponts, p² a vécu, grandi, jusqu'à fêter très discrètement ses 20 ans. Pourtant, fin 2024 avait germé dans les cerveaux vieillissants de ses fondateurs l’idée de célébrer en grande pompe ce bel âge à l’occasion du retour en Ligue 1 de la bande à ODO. Le timing semblait idéal, le contexte constituant un joli clin d’œil aux débuts de notre aventure. Lors d’une réunion débridée et fertile, les idées les plus folles pour marquer joliment le coup jaillirent en feu d’artifices.

Las. En fait de fête, l’ASSE nous offrit une saison en forme de chemin de croix, douchant nos enthousiasmes, mouillant nos pétards, freinant nos résolutions, justifiant notre procrastination.

Témoignant de son amitié en nous invitant à combattre notre détresse, de là-haut, Thérèse nous glissa alors que notre site n’avait pas un physique facile et qu’il y a temps pour prendre ses aises, et un temps pour prendre sur soi. Vexés, mais consciencieux, nous finîmes par nous y coller. Peut-être parce que les renoncements de la veille sont les aigreurs du lendemain, sûrement parce qu’on se le devait, à nous, mais surtout à vous, la communauté potonaute, les fidèles compagnons de cette belle aventure.

Alors Veryvel a enfilé son tablier, pris ses plus beaux pinceaux, cherché en vain son vinyle de Bowie avant - faute de mieux - de glisser Zouk Machine dans son mange disque et a nettoyé, balayé et astiqué du sol au plafond, kaz la toujou penpan a-t-il cru bon d’ajouter.

Oui pimpant, clinquant, affriolant, fringant ! Voilà l'ambitieux programme pour la vitrine (le site) comme pour le cœur du réacteur (le forum).

Revoir la forme pour mieux servir le fond, telle est l’intention.

Mais rassurez-vous s’il s’offre un lifting pour ses 20 piges, poteaux-carrés - revisitant le concept malmené du en même temps - change et reste le même. Dit autrement, comme le beau – oui – David, il se réinvente mais se reste fidèle : même ripoliné jusque dans les coins, poteaux-carrés est toujours préparé et emballé par des passionnés pour des passionnés. Certains s’en souviennent peut-être, il y a 21 ans, nous écrivions pour nous présenter que nous avions tout à la fois :

- le souci de vivre notre passion des Verts au présent tout en laissant au passé la place d’honneur qu’il mérite,

- le vœu de vivre notre passion dans la joie, la bonne humeur, la gaudriole,

- la folle prétention d’être décalé et drôle,

- la volonté d’être le plus nombreux possible pour prolonger les (d)ébats jusqu’au bout de la nuit, sur le forum ou sur le zinc, clavier au bout des doigts ou binouze à la main.

Si l'enveloppe s'est flétrie et méritait son lifting, notre vocation n'a pas pris une ride. Parce que, comme à l'époque, comme toujours, nous continuons de rêver à ce jour où le ballon caressera le poteau dans le bon sens, et rebondira du bon côté de la ligne, verte, forcément.

Réagir sur le forumLe débat continue entre potonautes.

L'exemple type d'une belle victoire sans lendemain, symbole de l'ASSE des années 90...

#2443. Provedel e l’Inter: «Un sogno che si realizza». Il ricordo di Toldo

Il portiere ammette l’incredulità iniziale e racconta la sua reazione da bambino al gol dell’idolo contro la Juve.

Ivan Provedel ha raccontato il suo trasferimento estivo dalla Lazio all’Inter nella quarta puntata di Welcome Kit, il format di Inter TV powered by Betsson Sport. Il portiere ha parlato della chiamata ricevuta dai nerazzurri, dell’obiettivo che si è dato nella nuova squadra e del ricordo di Toldo, il suo idolo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il contatto dell’Inter ha colto Provedel di sorpresa: «Quando mi ha chiamato l’Inter sono stato un po’ incredulo». A quella prima reazione non è seguita subito la certezza del trasferimento. Il portiere ha spiegato di aver aspettato che l’operazione fosse conclusa prima di lasciarsi andare all’entusiasmo: «fino a che non ho firmato non ho voluto pensare o illudermi, fino a che non è stato tutto fatto». Solo dopo la firma, ha raccontato, è stato felicissimo.

Provedel ha indicato anche quale sia il suo primo obiettivo da interista: «Dimostrare che qui ci posso stare e che posso dare il mio contributo alla squadra». Alla domanda su che cosa rappresenti per lui indossare la maglia del club, ha risposto: «Un sogno che si realizza».

Nelle sue parole, l’attesa prudente prima della firma lascia spazio alla felicità per il passaggio all’Inter. Provedel ha collegato l’arrivo in nerazzurro al desiderio di dare un contributo alla squadra, oltre che al significato personale della maglia che ora indossa.

#2442. 2. Bundesliga: Magdeburg thrash St. Pauli 4-1 to move up to 4th in the table

The hosts made a bright start and were rewarded for their early pressure in the 27th minute. Following a short corner routine involving Baris Atik and Alexander Nollenberger, Torben Müsel played the ball into the path of Mateusz Żukowski, who unleashed a powerful effort from distance into the top-right corner to give Magdeburg the lead.

St. Pauli struggled to find a response before the interval, with Magdeburg looking the more dangerous side. The visitors had opportunities of their own, but the hosts went into the break with a deserved advantage.

Magdeburg wasted little time extending their lead after the restart, with Anselmo García MacNulty making it 2-0 in the 48th minute. The defender found the net with a left-footed effort to put the hosts firmly in control.

However, St. Pauli responded ten minutes later when Eric Smith pulled one back in the 58th minute. The defender rose highest to head home Branimir Hrgota’s delivery, giving the visitors renewed hope of getting something from the encounter.

The visitors subsequently looked to build on their momentum, but Magdeburg remained organised and managed to keep their opponents at bay as the game entered its closing stages.

Any hopes of a St. Pauli comeback were ended in the 89th minute when Herbert Bockhorn restored Magdeburg’s two-goal advantage. Roko Simić then added further gloss to the scoreline with another late strike, completing a convincing 4-1 victory for the hosts.

The result represents another important three points for Petrik Sander’s side, who continue to establish themselves among the promotion contenders. St. Pauli, meanwhile, have now suffered consecutive league defeats following last weekend’s 3-1 loss to Nürnberg.

#2441. Vignes espère grappiller au moins un point

Entraîneur de la plus mauvaise équipe à l'extérieur de Ligue 2 (1 points sur 15), le Lavallois David Vignes (53 ans) s'est exprimé en conférence de presse avant d'affronter demain soir dans le Chaudron des leaders stéphanois intraitables à la maison depuis le début de saison (5 victoires en 5 matches). Extraits.

"Saint-Etienne, Geoffroy Guichard, ça m'évoque beaucoup de souvenirs, même si j'étais très jeune à la fin des années 70. Mais évidemment, tout le monde en parlait. Au début des années 80, c'était le club phare, un peu le PSG d'aujourd'hui, avec d'autres valeurs, avec d'autres moyens. Les Verts, ça a bercé mon enfance. J'ai beaucoup vu d'images, j'ai entendu beaucoup de chansons qui ont aussi dicté mon enfance. Lorsque j'ai démarré le foot à 6 ans, très tôt, j'ai eu un maillot de Saint-Etienne à mettre sur mes épaules aux entraînements. Le fameux Manufrance, Le Coq sportif…

Les Verts, c'est beaucoup de souvenirs, un club mythique de notre patrimoine footballistique. Bon, aujourd'hui, un club se trouvant en Ligue 2… Je n'ai pas les yeux de l'enfant qui rêvait devant ces images. C'est aussi de la fierté de pouvoir mener un club, une équipe à jouer dans ce stade-là, face à cette équipe-là. Avec vraiment l'ambition de leur rendre la tâche difficile, d'aller essayer de prendre quelque chose, au moins un point. D’autant plus que c'est un stade que je n'ai jamais vu de match là-bas. Je l'ai visité, mais vide. Là, je vais voir un match de très près. C'est top !

Les Verts ont remporté tous leurs matches à domicile, on n’a pris qu’un point à l’extérieur ? Quand on présente le match comme ça, il est totalement déséquilibré, évidemment, même si la dernière journée, ils ont perdu, nous, on a gagné. Donc, on leur a pris trois points (sourire). Mais non, c'est une équipe qui, pour l'instant, est leader. Sans l'ombre d'un doute, en fait ! C'est vrai qu'ils ont eu cette défaite avec un très bon match des Guingampais. J'ai vu que le coach de Saint-Etienne a attribué ça à la thèse de l'accident. On va faire en sorte que ce soit peut-être un peu plus qu'un accident. Mais on sait que ça va être très, très difficile.

Nous, c'est vrai qu'on n'a pas pris de points à l'extérieur encore. Enfin si, un à Metz tout de même. Mais on a fait cependant des matchs très cohérents à l'extérieur. Et dans la dynamique des récents matchs, j'ai bon espoir qu'on obtienne quelque chose. En affichant la solidité démontrée au moins sur les deux derniers matchs. Il va falloir qu'on soit très discipliné, très rigoureux tout au long du match. Mais effectivement, sans trop se renier, si on doit leur poser des problèmes, c'est aussi en pouvant utiliser le ballon de la meilleure des manières. Et ça, on a quand même posé des problèmes à plusieurs adversaires. Même à l'extérieur.

Même si l'ambiance sera tout autre, j'espère vraiment que mes joueurs vont faire preuve de grande personnalité pour pouvoir leur poser des problèmes dans notre utilisation du ballon. Parce que c'est une équipe qui l'utilise bien. Ils savent aussi faire le dos rond, ils savent défendre. Mais je pense qu'ils préfèrent avoir le ballon que défendre malgré tout. Il y aura des moments charnières dans ce match qu'il faudra bien négocier. Mais il faudra qu'on soit très bons dans ce que l'on fait, dans ce qu'on essaie de faire avec le ballon. Et j'espère vraiment qu'on pourra le démontrer demain.

Si c’est un match bonus ? Ce qui serait bonus, c'est si on obtenait un résultat. Parce que peu d'équipes ont pris des points contre Saint-Etienne. Dunkerque et Guingamp en ont pris trois. Et Metz en a pris un. Après, pour tous les autres, ça a été difficile. Mais là, je ne le considère pas comme un match de gala ou de bonus. Non, c'est ce que j'ai déjà dit aux joueurs et que je vais répéter en fin de journée. Pour nous, notre premier enjeu, c'est de continuer et de valider cette victoire enfin obtenue contre Boulogne. Ce premier clean sheet. L'enjeu est là, c'est de continuer. Ça tombe sur un déplacement à Geoffroy-Guichard. Evidemment, ce n'est pas chose aisée. Mais est-ce qu'il y a vraiment des matchs plus faciles que d'autres ? Je n'en suis pas certain.

Quand on présente comme ça un déplacement à Saint-Etienne qui presque survole le championnat, ce n'est pas facile. Peu d'équipes ont pris des points aux Verts mais il y en a certaines qui ont réussi. Et le football, encore une fois, permet ça. Et donc, pourquoi pas l'avoir à Saint-Etienne ? En tout cas, mon discours sera là. Encore une fois, avec beaucoup d'humilité. Pas question de se prendre pour d'autres sous prétexte qu'on a gagné contre Boulogne. Pas du tout. Mais je sais qu'on peut leur poser des problèmes. Je sais que ça va être difficile. Ça va être très difficile par moments. Mais tout est possible. Et je veux qu'on y aille avec cette ambition-là. Mais ce n'est pas le match de gala, le match bonus. Pas du tout.

Moi, j'aimerais qu'on continue et qu'on enchaîne après cette victoire contre Boulogne, acquise dans la difficulté malgré tout. Mais si on peut aller prendre au moins un point dans la difficulté à Saint-Etienne, ça ne fera que renforcer notre dynamique. Et là, je vois une simple victoire contre Boulogne, tout ce que ça peut amener, engendrer comme soulagement, comme bien-être, même si avant ça, malgré les défaites, l'ambiance était bonne, le travail était bien, le climat, tout était positif. Mais là, on voit de suite qu'une seule victoire, même difficilement acquise, ça nous fait sauter deux places déjà. Et on veut continuer là-dessus."

#2440. Saint-Etienne, ça fait plus rêver que les autres équipes

Auteur du but égalisateur des Lavallois contre les Verts à Francis Le Basser lors de la première journée de la saison dernière, le Lavallois Ethan Clavreul (20 ans) se réjouit d'être dans le groupe lavallois qui débarquera demain soir dans le Chaudron, comme il l'a expliqué en conférence de presse.

"La saison passée, j'avais vu à la télé le match à Saint-Etienne. Franchement, c'est beau à voir. Même quand tu regardes leurs matchs, il y a toujours une ambiance, il y a une ferveur, il y a un truc. Après moi, quand je rentre sur le terrain, je fais abstraction des tribunes. Peut-être qu'il y aura du bruit, il y aura du monde. Tant que tu fais un bon match, que tu joues, c'est le principal. Franchement, contre Saint-Etienne à Laval, c'était un sentiment particulier parce que c'est mon premier match, mon premier but. Mais là, ça fait 6 gros mois que je suis dans le monde du foot pro. Je sais ce que c'est les ambiances. Franchement, oui, ça peut être impressionnant au début, mais une fois que l'échauffement commence, je suis dans ma bulle et je ne regarde pas trop autour.

Sportivement, quand on affronte une équipe qui n'a pas lâché un point à domicile, comment arrive-t-on à se dire qu'il y a quelque chose à aller chercher là-bas ? On sait qu'on a des armes, ils ont des faiblesses. Ils ont des armes, on a aussi des faiblesses, comme toute équipe. Après, on l'a bien vu, vendredi dernier contre Boulogne, si on est un peu moins beau, ce n'est pas grave. L'objectif, c'est de gagner des matchs. En vrai, on a des armes qui peuvent les embêter comme eux ont des armes pour nous embêter. Je pense que si on est un peu plus mordants qu'eux, on peut les surprendre là-bas et faire un bon coup dans la tête et au classement aussi.

Je pense que le fait qu’ils aient perdu leur dernier match, ça a dû les piquer. Je pense qu'ils se sont dit que la saison n'était pas finie. Ça fait une petite piqûre de rappel. C'est toujours bien pour toute équipe qui gagne beaucoup de matchs à domicile ou à l'extérieur. Nous, on sait qu'ils ont perdu. On sait qu'ils vont être revanchards pour leur public parce que pour eux, c'est interdit de perdre deux fois d'affilée. Nous, on sait qu'on vient d'avoir une victoire à domicile. Nous, on a envie d'emmener le public avec nous. On les a emmenés un peu à Boulogne. Si on gagne à Saint-Etienne, je pense que contre Montpellier, il y aura un peu plus de monde dans les tribunes et un peu plus de bruit.

Quand je savais que Saint-Etienne était encore dans notre championnat, quand on l'a vu, que nous restions aussi dans ce championnat-là, je me dis que ce match-là, à l'extérieur, il faut que j'y aille. L'année dernière, je ne l'ai pas fait. J'étais dégoûté. Toute ma famille avait fait le déplacement. Quand je les appelle, je dis que je ne suis pas dans le groupe. Ce n'était pas extraordinaire. Donc, cette année, je me suis dit que toute la saison, je vais prendre le match par match. Saint-Etienne, ça fait toujours un peu plus rêver que les autres équipes. Ce n'est pas pour autant que je néglige toutes les autres équipes. C'est que Saint-Etienne, il y a une ferveur, il y a un truc. Personnellement, jouer des matchs avec beaucoup d'ambiance, beaucoup de monde au stade, des gros stades comme ça… Oui, ça fait toujours un petit truc dans sa tête !"

#2437. 2. Bundesliga: Bochum snatch dramatic late victory over Karlsruher SC

The hosts made an electric start and needed just six minutes to take the lead. Berkan Taz picked out Christian Rasmussen on the left-hand side of the penalty area, with the Danish forward taking aim and firing a superb effort into the far corner beyond Hans Christian Bernat.

However, Karlsruhe responded almost immediately. Just two minutes later, Marvin Wanitzek teed up Kevin Wiethaup on the edge of the penalty area, and the midfielder produced an equally impressive finish into the top corner to restore parity.

Bochum subsequently enjoyed more possession and looked the more threatening side, with Karol Mets going closest to restoring their advantage. The defender was unable to convert from close range after Philipp Hofmann had nodded the ball into his path, while Jarne Steuckers also tested Bernat with a powerful effort from outside the box.

Despite the hosts’ pressure, Karlsruhe remained organised and managed to keep the score level heading into the interval.

The visitors made a flying start to the second half and took the lead just five minutes after the restart. Following a Bochum corner, Shio Fukuda helped keep the ball alive before Tim Civeja spotted Timo Horn off his line and produced a sensational strike from around the halfway line, sending the ball over the goalkeeper and into the net to make it 2-1.

Bochum responded almost immediately, however, with Hofmann bringing the hosts level in the 53rd minute. After Taz delivered the ball into the penalty area, Rasmussen helped it into the path of the former Karlsruhe striker, who made no mistake from close range.

Both sides subsequently searched for a winner, with Bochum coming particularly close through Taz and Hofmann in the 74th minute. Bernat initially parried Taz’s effort before producing an outstanding reaction save to deny Hofmann from the rebound.

The Karlsruhe goalkeeper continued to frustrate the hosts as the game entered its closing stages, while Bochum also had to remain alert to the visitors’ counter-attacking threat.

However, Uwe Rösler’s side eventually found their breakthrough in the second minute of stoppage time. After Mansour Ouro-Tagba drove forward down the left, Hofmann helped the ball back into the path of Taz, whose effort was saved by Bernat. The resulting attack remained alive, and Karol Mets delivered the decisive ball into the penalty area for Hofmann to finish from close range and complete a remarkable comeback.

The late winner sparked celebrations around the Vonovia Ruhrstadion, with Bochum claiming all three points in an entertaining five-goal encounter.

The victory continues Bochum’s recent improvement under Rösler, while Karlsruhe will be left frustrated after twice taking the lead and ultimately coming away empty-handed.

#2432. England’s Dutch coach Sarina Wiegman extends contract until 2029

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Dutch football coach Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract with the England women’s team by two years, taking her up to the 2029 European Championships.

Wiegman, 56, led the team to two European titles in 2022 and 2025, as well as their first World Cup final in 2023, when they lost to Spain.

Prior to that she won the European Championships with the Dutch national team in 2017 and reached the World Cup final two years later, losing 2-0 to the United States.

“I am so happy to be able to carry on with this squad and cannot think of a better job in football,” she said in a statement released by the English Football Association (FA).

“Working for a world-class organisation like the FA, and alongside so many people dedicated to winning England teams and the growth of our game, excites me every day.”

FA chief executive Mark Bullingham described Wiegman as “an incredible coach with an unparalleled record in major tournaments”. He added: “There is no one better to lead the Lionesses into the next two tournaments.”

Commentators had widely expected the Dutchwoman to leave her post after next year’s World Cup, after England failed to qualify automatically for the tournament.

A 4-0 loss to Spain in June, the team’s heaviest defeat since Wiegman took charge, means they will have to come through a play-off tournament with Greece, Ukraine and Slovakia to reach the finals in Brazil.

Wiegman said: “Anyone who knows me will understand that my main concern right now is absolutely the World Cup, and helping this squad realise their potential in the years to come.

“We have an important job to do to confirm our place in Brazil, and hopefully we can do that and give the country another special summer to remember next year.”

#2429. Briançon prépare sa reconversion

Valeureux et heureux capitaine d'un Pau FC 5e de L2 et restant sur une série de 5 succès consécutifs avant de recevoir ce soir les Canaris 5 semaines avant d'accueillir les Verts, l'ancien défenseur stéphanois Anthony Briançon, qui fêtera ses 32 ans dans 3 semaines, a évoqué en début de semaine sa reconversion sur son compte LinkedIn.

"À la base, j’ai créé un compte LinkedIn parce que c’était un exercice demandé pendant ma formation à l'EM Lyon Business School . Je ne pensais pas forcément que ce réseau aurait un véritable intérêt pour moi. Et puis, en avançant dans ma réflexion sur l’après-carrière, j’ai compris quelque chose : préparer la suite ne commence pas le jour où l’on arrête de jouer.

Aujourd’hui, je suis encore pleinement footballeur. J’ai encore des objectifs, des matchs à jouer et beaucoup de choses à vivre sur les terrains. Mais en parallèle, je me forme au scouting, à la data et au métier de directeur sportif. Et pourquoi pas, à terme, passer aussi mes diplômes d’entraîneur.

Après des années passées dans les vestiaires, sur les terrains et au contact de nombreux entraîneurs, dirigeants et joueurs, forcément, on développe un regard différent sur le football. Être capitaine pendant plusieurs années m’a aussi beaucoup appris sur l’humain, l’écoute et l’importance de faire avancer un groupe ensemble.

On apprend à observer un joueur au-delà de ses qualités techniques, à comprendre sa personnalité, ce qu’il peut apporter humainement à un groupe, mais aussi l’importance du partage, de la transmission et des relations que l’on construit au quotidien. Mais l’expérience du terrain ne suffit pas. C’est justement pour ça que j’ai envie de la compléter aujourd’hui

Par de nouvelles compétences, de nouvelles méthodes et une autre manière d’analyser le jeu. Je ne sais pas encore exactement où cette deuxième partie de carrière me mènera. En revanche, je sais dans quelle direction j’ai envie d’avancer. Et je trouve finalement assez logique de commencer à la construire pendant que je joue encore. La carrière de joueur a une fin. La passion du football, beaucoup moins."

#2428. Nesta e i derby: "A Roma ho fatto i danni, soffrivo troppo. A Milano giocavo in scioltezza"

L'ex capitano biancoceleste racconta le forti emozioni vissute nelle stracittadine del passato e presenta il derby contro il Benevento sulla panchina dell'Avellino

Alla vigilia del sentito derby di Serie B tra Benevento e Avellino, l'allenatore biancoverde Alessandro Nesta fa il punto sulle sue emozioni. Mettendo a confronto la sfida con la sua celebre esperienza vissuta nella capitale, l'ex capitano biancoceleste spiega come il derby contro la Roma rappresentasse per lui una grandissima pressione e una fonte di ansia immensa, vissuta ben diversamente rispetto alla tranquillità del derby tra Inter e Milan.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

I derby? In quelli di Roma ho fatti i danni. Essendo la mia città lo soffrivo troppo. Nessun'altra partita, neppure la finale di Champions League, mi ha mai trasmesso una simile ansia. Quelli di Milano li ho giocati in scioltezza. Uno l'ho perfino giocato in occasione di una semifinale di Champions, ma il giorno dopo ero in bicicletta a Corso Vercelli. Un altro mondo.

Da allenatore il derby lo sento. Non come quello di Roma, ma lo sento. So che è una partita importante. So come si sente la gente, perché sono stato anche tifoso. So che dobbiamo andare a fare una partita vera. Trasferta vietata? I derby devono avere entrambe le tifoserie. A noi mancherà qualcosa, ma questo deve darci forza. Dobbiamo andare a lottare: per noi e per loro, che non potranno esserci.

#2427. 2. Bundesliga: Heidenheim and Hannover share the points in four-goal thriller

The visitors made the brighter start and came close to opening the scoring inside the opening 15 minutes. Benjamin Källman did well to get in behind the Heidenheim defence before pulling the ball back for Husseyn Chakroun, who somehow missed the target with the goal at his mercy.

Hannover continued to look dangerous, with Marcel Hartel and Stefán Teitur Thórdarson also threatening, while Heidenheim struggled to create much of note in the opening stages.

Despite the visitors looking the more likely to score, it was Frank Schmidt’s side who broke the deadlock shortly before half-time. A long-range free-kick from Paul Hennrich caused problems inside the Hannover penalty area, with Jean Hugonet inadvertently diverting the ball into the path of Tim Siersleben, who reacted quickest to head home from close range in the 43rd minute.

Heidenheim therefore went into the interval with a somewhat fortunate 1-0 advantage, despite Hannover having created the better opportunities during the opening 45 minutes.

Sandro Wagner’s side came out with renewed purpose after the restart and were rewarded for their efforts in the 55th minute. Källman picked out Thórdarson on the edge of the penalty area, with the midfielder producing a precise first-time finish into the bottom-right corner to bring Hannover level.

The visitors continued to build momentum and completed the turnaround just eight minutes later. Marcel Hartel delivered a dangerous corner into the penalty area, where Hugonet rose highest to power a header beyond Thomas Dähne and put Hannover 2-1 ahead in the 63rd minute.

However, their advantage lasted less than three minutes. Heidenheim responded through a corner of their own, with substitute Christian Conteh delivering an inviting ball towards the near post for Budu Zivzivadze to glance a header into the net and restore parity at 2-2.

Both sides subsequently pushed for a winner in an increasingly open encounter. Hannover continued to threaten through Chakroun, while Heidenheim looked to take advantage of their attacking momentum following the equaliser.

Neither side could find a decisive breakthrough during the closing stages, however, with the points ultimately shared after an entertaining afternoon in Heidenheim.

The result extends Heidenheim’s winless run, while Hannover will take encouragement from their second-half response after coming from behind to take the lead, even if they were unable to hold on for all three points.

PSV survived a second-half onslaught in Porto to secure their first win of the Champions League group stages.

The Eindhoven club were worth their narrow lead against Francesco Farioli’s side after dominating possession in the first half, but rarely troubled Diogo Costa in the Porto goal.

At the other end, substitute Denis Man came close to scoring a second for PSV with his first touch when his curling shot beat Costa but failed to sneak inside the post.

The 1-0 win lifts PSV to a provisional 16th place in the Champions League table at the halfway stage of round three, while Porto are still looking for their first point.

Their next match is at home to Belgian side Club Brugge, who will make the short trip to Eindhoven on November 4.

#2425. Top five football betting tips and tricks

Football is the world’s most famous sport, and it is the sport of choice of a great many sports punters as well. Especially popular in Europe, betting on football can be an incredibly profitable enterprise, so long as you know how to do it.

Getting started on football betting is far from easy, though. This form of gambling requires dedication, investment, and persistence. As you gain experience, your intuition will improve and you will be able to make more correct predictions.

But experience is not the only thing that can help you become a better football punter. In fact, you can substantially improve your betting strategy by simply following some basic football betting tips.

You might find shopping around boring and unhelpful, but you just have to do it when you search sites for football betting. As you know, the higher the odds, the bigger the payout. What you may have missed, however, is that odds are different at each bookmaker. Having said that, shopping around for the best odds is sensible, as it rewards you with bigger payouts.

In this line of thought, sticking to one bookmaker is virtually pointless. Even if the bookie of your choosing offers the best odds for a number of matches, it is highly unlikely that their odds will remain the best for long.

An obvious one, we know. And yet, you will be surprised by the number of football bettors who wager on football, but do not follow the sport. So, why is it important to follow the action closely?

First of all, by watching football matches, you can take part in the most exciting football betting market – the live betting market. What is more important, however, is that following the action provides an invaluable insight into teams and players’ style, condition, and determination – important factors  to consider when placing a bet.

As you watch more and more games, you will improve your analytic abilities. In time, you will be able to make more accurate predictions about the outcome of different matches, which, of course,  will result in placing more winning bets.

As you know, odds are based on the probability of occurrence of a certain outcome; the higher the odds, the more unlikely it is for that outcome to actually occur. But what happens when the odds offered by the bookmaker represent a probability that is lower than the actual probability of an outcome occurring? In such a situation, you can place what is called a value bet.

If you want to become a professional football punter, you should always search for value when betting, as it leads to huge profits

Favoured by beginners in particular, accumulators are a type of football wager which allows you to bet on as many fixtures as you like. Most commonly, you will be asked to choose a match winner, but as the market is diverse, you may be offered a number of other betting options. What makes accumulators an appealing betting market is the huge potential payout – here, you can stake as little as £1 and have the potential to win more than £500,000, depending on the bookmaker and the number of selected fixtures.

If you find accumulators’ payouts too good to be true, you are right. As a matter of fact, there is a reason for the odds to be set so high – actually winning an accumulator bet, especially one which involves a wide selection of matches, is nearly impossible. You see, all you need for your whole wager to lose is one wrong prediction. For example, if you bet on 10 matches and just one of them goes wrong, your entire accumulator is lost.

To make money by betting on football, avoid betting on accumulators – the risk is simply not worth it.

Finally, if you want to be a successful football punter, learn how not to mix emotions with betting. This is easier said than done, though.

Whenever your favourite team plays, you want them to win, regardless of how (im)possible that may be. If you do not learn how to leave emotions out of betting, however, you are highly likely to put money on your favourite team even if they have no chance of winning the match. Conversely, should you base your bets on hard facts and not on emotions, you increase your chances to win.

Our advice – avoid betting on fixtures that involve one of your favourite teams, that is the easiest way to keep emotions at bay.
